labels.label: T-abs-omega-one-constant (no paper label; the roadmap title and evidence, programme/roadmap.toml:1016-1028)
labels.notes: Nothing is marked, and nothing should be: there is no paper and no ledger row. The docstring's bold items (Continuity at limits, The general theorem, At ω₁, Each hypothesis is needed, no label is marked) hold no backticked label. The docstring quotes the roadmap title's first sentence verbatim (:17-19) and the evidence's 'Optionally ...' sentence verbatim (:21). (1) THE ω₁ FORM. exists_forall_ge_eq_of_continuous_omega_one (:281): for g : Iio (ω₁ : Ordinal.{u}) → Y with Continuous g, [T1Space Y] and [SecondCountableTopology Y], it gives ∃ γ, ∀ a, γ ≤ a → g a = g γ. That is the target's sentence, and it is universe-polymorphic. With pp.universes, ω₁ elaborates to Ordinal.omega.{u} 1. Mathlib's docstring says this is the first uncountable ordinal (Mathlib/SetTheory/Cardinal/Aleph.lean:200, 211-212: scoped notation ω₁ => ω_ 1). The topology is the order topology of ω₁. Ordinal carries Preorder.topology with OrderTopology ⟨rfl⟩ (Mathlib/SetTheory/Ordinal/Topology.lean:42-43). On an OrdConnected subset of a linear order with the order topology, the subspace topology is the order topology of the induced order: instance orderTopology_of_ordConnected (Mathlib/Topology/Order/Basic.lean:341), which #synth OrderTopology (Set.Iio (Ordinal.omega 1)) returns. Iio is OrdConnected, and Iio ω₁ with the induced order is the order type ω₁. So the subtype is ω₁ with its order topology. (2) THE GENERAL THEOREM. LimitContinuous.exists_forall_ge_eq (:209) takes any LinearOrder with WellFoundedLT, ℵ₀ < Order.cof α (Mathlib's least cardinality of a cofinal set, Cofinality/Basic.lean:35), [T1Space Y], [SecondCountableTopology Y] and LimitContinuous g, and gives ∃ γ, ∀ a ≥ γ, g a = g γ. That is the evidence's optional form. LimitContinuous (:94) says: at every IsSuccLimit a, every U ∈ 𝓝 (g a) has b < a with g c ∈ U for all c in (b, a). That is the target's 'equivalently'. continuous_iff_limitContinuous (:109) is correct as stated, under [LinearOrder] [WellFoundedLT] [TopologicalSpace] [OrderTopology]. At a non-limit point (IsMin, or a covers a point), 𝓝[<] a = ⊥. At every point, 𝓝[>] a = ⊥ (IsMax, or exists_covBy_of_wellFoundedLT). So continuity is left continuity at successor limits. limitContinuous_of_continuous needs only a linear order. (3) VARIANTS. _of_separating (:148): a countable ι with B i open and ∀ x ≠ y, ∃ i, x ∈ B i ∧ y ∉ B i. Such a family generates exactly a coarser T1, second countable topology, as claimed. Openness is used (hB i).mem_nhds. _of_injective (:223): a continuous injection into a T1, second countable Z. _of_cof_ne_aleph0 (:249): [Nonempty α] and cof ≠ ℵ₀. The case cof ≤ 1 is Order.cof_le_one_iff, a top. Otherwise ℵ₀ ≤ cof by Order.aleph0_le_cof_iff. The forms exists_forall_ge_eq_of_continuous, eventuallyConst_atTop_of_continuous (Filter.EventuallyConst g atTop), exists_lt_omega_one_forall_eq (the limit condition inline, on g : Ordinal.{u} → Y read below ω₁), _of_tendsto (Tendsto g (𝓝[<] a) (𝓝 (g a)) at limits a < ω₁) and _of_continuousOn (ContinuousOn g (Iio ω₁)) each conclude ∃ γ < ω₁, ∀ a, γ ≤ a → a < ω₁ → g a = g γ, or the subtype form. exists_lt_omega_one_forall_eq turns the Ordinal-level limit condition into LimitContinuous on the subtype. It uses IsSuccLimit.subtypeVal with isLowerSet_Iio, which is the needed direction. (4) THE FAMILY FORM, exists_lt_omega_one_forall_eq_family (:320): ι : Type v countable, g : ι → Ordinal.{u} → Y, each g i under the inline limit condition below ω₁. It gives one γ < ω₁ with g i a = g i γ for all i and all a ∈ [γ, ω₁). The bound is the sup of the countably many γ i, below ω₁ by Ordinal.iSup_lt_omega_one (Regular.lean:100). That is what T-abs-curves-extend-second-countable (2b) needs. (5) VACUITY. None. ℵ₀ < cof holds at Iio ω₁ (aleph0_lt_cof_Iio_omega_one). Constant maps into ℝ satisfy every hypothesis. The separating family exists for any T1, second countable Y (it is how exists_forall_ge_eq is derived). (6) SHARPNESS. nat_separates is a well order of cofinality ℵ₀ (Order.cof_nat) with no successor limits, so every map is LimitContinuous. Its identity into discrete ℕ (T2, second countable) is not eventually constant, which refutes cofinality ℵ₀. sierpinski_separates uses Prop with Mathlib's only topology, sierpinskiSpace = generateFrom {{True}}, which is T0 and second countable (finite). Its g a = ¬ IsSuccLimit a is continuous: the preimage of {True} is the set of isolated non-limit points, open by SuccOrder.isOpen_singleton_iff. It is not eventually constant: γ + 1 and γ + ω lie in every tail (Ordinal.isPrincipal_add_omega). So T1 cannot be weakened to T0; that Prop is not T1 then follows from the theorem. omega_one_id_separates: Iio ω₁ is T2 (instance) and first countable (firstCountableTopology_Iio_omega_one: the intervals (b, a] with b < a, countably many by countable_Iio_of_lt_omega_one, plus 𝓝[>] a = ⊥). Its identity, continuous, is not eventually constant (succ γ < ω₁). So first countability with T2 does not replace second countability. Each counterexample shows what it claims. SCOPE's two unformalized remarks are true. The first holds with blocks (a_n, a_{n+1}], which are clopen in any well order; with [a_n, a_{n+1}) one must take the a_n non-limit. The second holds because ω₁ + 1 is compact T2 and the inclusion is not eventually constant. One correction, finding 1: T0Space Prop IS derivable in Mathlib at this pin.

findings.where: lean-causal/campaign/T-abs-omega-one-constant/REPORT.json witness ('t0Space_prop, not a Mathlib instance at this pin') and kb_proposals[2] ('T0Space Prop is not an instance, use Causal.t0Space_prop'); lean-causal/scaffold/CausalScaffold/OmegaOneConstant.lean:351
findings.what: Mathlib does not lack it. Mathlib/Topology/Order/LowerUpperTopology.lean:551 declares `instance : IsUpper Prop` (the Sierpiński topology is the upper topology). With :451, `instance (priority := 90) t0Space : T0Space α` for IsUpper, it gives T0Space Prop by instance search. A probe that imports only Mathlib.Topology.Order.LowerUpperTopology gets `#synth T0Space Prop` = Topology.IsUpper.t0Space, exit 0, since deleted. The instance is missing only from this file's import set. Causal.t0Space_prop is correct but duplicates Mathlib, and the proposed kb pitfall would teach the next session a falsehood.
findings.fix: Reword kb_proposals[2] and the witness text: 'T0Space Prop is Topology.IsUpper.t0Space, found by instance search once Mathlib.Topology.Order.LowerUpperTopology is imported'. Optionally, import that module and prove t0Space_prop by inferInstance, or drop it in favour of the instance.

findings.where: lean-causal/campaign/T-abs-omega-one-constant/REPORT.json notes, item 5(a) (with (c)); inherited from the step (2b) sketch in programme/roadmap.toml (T-abs-curves-extend-second-countable evidence)
findings.what: Note 5(a) says the final segment 'is non-degenerate by the right excess'. That fails when the excess is a single point. Note 5(c) derives cofinal right excesses from 'not onto', so an excess there means only some point of I_j above the image of I_i. That point can be just the added endpoint, e.g. a tail-free curve over [0, 1) extended to [0, 1] by its limit. φ is id, the image [0, 1) is ordconnected, and both curves are tail-free. If i_{α+1} is such an extension of i_α, then s_α = max I_{i_{α+1}}. In the coordinates of I_{i_{α+2}}, s_{α+1} is the image of s_α. So (s_α, s_{α+1}) is empty, the points s_α^q cannot be chosen, and there is no non-degenerate final segment to contradict tail-freeness. The sketch's 'take a point s_α^q in (s_α, s_{α+1})' has the same gap. The fix is cheap, so (2b) is not blocked. Take i_{α+1} two right-excess steps above i_α: j with an excess t_j over i_α, then k with an excess t_k over j. Then the sup s of the image of I_{i_α} in I_k satisfies s ≤ φ_{jk}(t_j) < t_k, a non-degenerate excess. Two smaller slips in the same note. The successor used is α + 1 (its points lie in (s_{α+1}, s_{α+2})), so the condition should be α + 1 ≥ γ, not α + 2 ≥ γ. And 'constant on a dense subset' needs the s_α^q chosen dense, e.g. s_α + q (s_{α+1} − s_α) in the coordinates of I_{i_{α+2}}. Density then survives the carrying maps, which are homeomorphisms onto intervals. Notes 4, 5(b), (c), (d) and (e) are otherwise sound. In (b), at a limit λ, s_λ (the sup of the earlier carried points) lies in I_{i_{λ+1}} below the right end of the image of I_{i_λ}, and the squeeze gives the inline ∃ b < λ condition, limits c < λ included. In (c), an excess over i passes down to every i' ≤ i, so if neither kind of excess is cofinal, the larger witness is onto every later member.
findings.fix: For the consumer's closer, in notes 5 or the consumer's evidence: define the recursion's 'right excess' as non-degenerate (two points of I_j above the image, obtained by composing two point excesses), choose s_α^q dense, and read 'α + 1 ≥ γ'.
